values: Materials and setup｜entirely editorially designed fictitious courses

You are designing a lesson on 'Introduction to Exercise and Health' for a fictitious university, with 24 students, and the teaching audience has no real personal information. It must combine theoretical explanation with low-intensity activity; all dates, venues, grading, and safety conditions are for practice only.

A1｜Course on 2026-10-06 from 09:00 to 09:50: the learning objectives are to explain the difference between heart rate and rating of perceived exertion (RPE) and to state two exercise risk signals. The lesson plan must include 20 minutes of theory, 20 minutes of low-intensity activity, and 10 minutes of review; the activity must not require students to disclose health information to the whole class.

A2｜Venue confirmation on 2026-10-03: the original exercise room has a capacity of 30 and can hold 24; a projector and soft mats are available. The school requires checking the venue, equipment, and an alternative teaching plan before the activity. Students who feel unwell may choose observation and written reflection, and the teacher does not make medical judgments.

A3｜The grading rubric totals 10 points: 4 for explaining concepts, 3 for the safety plan, 2 for citing sources, and 1 for reflection. Students may answer using anonymized fictitious cases; how unsubmitted work is handled and the review channel follow school rules and are not set by the exercise.

A4｜Venue notice at 16:00 on 2026-10-05: the floor of the original exercise room is slippery and clearance has not yet been confirmed by the facilities manager. The October 6 course can move to an ordinary classroom, but the originally planned low-intensity activity cannot take place there; the ordinary classroom has a projector and holds up to 30.

A5｜Authorization chain: the teacher may adjust teaching activities and inform students; the facilities manager confirms venue safety; student illness is handled by on-campus health services under the procedure; grade disputes go through the course review channel. If the venue is still not cleared before class, stop the on-site activity first and submit the alternative lesson plan.
